says: Chowning's bell (1973): a carrier frequency-modulated by a modulator in the ratio 1:1.4, so the sidebands fall between the note's harmonics and the tone rings metallic; the modulation index starts high and decays with the amplitude, so the strike is bright and the tail thins to a few partials; no attack, a long decay, no sustain. In this engine: osc 1 is FM'd by osc 2 (osc_1_distortion_type 7), osc 2 a sine 5.825 semitones up (7:5), silent on its own; env 2 drives osc_1_distortion_amount down over the note; env 1 decays over seconds. What 'inharmonic' means here, measured 2026-09-14: 7:5 is a rational ratio, so every partial c(1 + 1.4k) sits on a grid five times finer than the note's harmonics - the render is periodic at the note's fifth (104.7 Hz under a C5 at 523), a fundamental nobody sounds; the harmonic-grid descriptors read it as perfectly harmonic (inharmonicity 0.002) against that low f0. The first version of this entry expected inharmonicity above 0.1 and was refuted; the signature the engine can check is the period far below the note (f0 at most a quarter of it), harmonic against that period, a bright strike (centroid 3.4 kHz) and the long decay.
